bug.title: The KS gate compares null roots with real roots, so genuine weak real edge voids campaigns; the gate must test whether nulls still behave like nulls
bug.symptoms: archC01–10 went VOID in 6 of 10 with nulls unchanged and real roots improved. archM01–25 (weaker reals) went VOID in 0 of 25. The gate rewards weaker research.
bug.reproduction_steps: Close out a synthetic Type-R campaign: - 5 null roots with IC t ~ N(0,1) - 25 real roots, each with a small true IC (t around 1, all below 2) The current gate voids it; the nulls are perfectly calibrated.
bug.expected: - **Gate A, null calibration (Type-R):** - Each null root contributes its ic_tstat. - A one-sample two-sided KS test against N(0,1) at α = 0.05 (an exact or asymptotic p, as nulloracle's ks module offers, or a documented one-sample implementation in closeout) decides VOID. - With fewer than 3 null roots, the gate is "insufficient", which is neither VOID nor ok. - **Gate A, Type-D:** the same test over the null-labelled nodes, one per branch (its shallowest null), labelled by the oracle's depth resolution. - **Gate B, agent behaviour:** a two-sided exact test (Fisher or permutation) comparing null and real roots on whether a root was selected for expansion in any round. It VOIDs only at p < 0.01, a stricter level, because it is a second gate. It is "insufficient" when no root was expanded. - **calibration_status:** - VOID if either gate rejects - ok if both are ok - otherwise insufficient VOID stays sticky, as CampaignVerdict already enforces. - **Diagnostics, never gating:** the previous root-nonsig null-vs-real KS p and the all-node KS p are still computed and reported. The JSON line carries: - ks_variant "null-calibration" - gate_a_p, gate_b_p - ks_pvalue_root_nonsig, ks_pvalue_all_nodes - the null t mean and sd, as aggregate numbers only - The persisted campaign_ks_guard p is gate A's. The rule and this spec's evidence are stated in the module docstring. - test_closeout_ks_null_calibration.py covers: - the reproduction above is ok - nulls with leaked edge (null t ~ N(1.5,1)) are VOID by gate A - nulls expanded far more often than reals are VOID by gate B - fewer than 3 null roots gives insufficient - a Type-D campaign - the diagnostics are reported It passes under pytest-xdist. - Existing close-out tests are updated only where they pin the old gate's sample; each keeps its intent. - The orchestrator member suite and root tests/ pass, including tests/e2e/test_planted_null_ks_guard.py. Its detectable-null case must still VOID under gate A.
bug.actual: Root cause: the gate's comparison includes real nodes, whose distribution moves with genuine edge, instead of testing the nulls against their own known distribution.
bug.constraints: nulloracle's KS functions are unchanged (call them or add the one-sample variant inside closeout) Null labels never leave the close-out process; only aggregate figures are printed No file outside the five listed is edited Do not edit docs/user-journeys/
